items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Rudy Wiedoft inspired them... Oh, definitely. He let you know what could be done on the instrument... It was purely technique, which was a dazzling technique for the time.

ctx.x: Well, you know, I can’t remember that there was anybody that influenced me. I know that I used to like the sound of Wayne King, the instrument, you know, the sound he got out of the instrument, and he was the melody player. Gee, I don’t know.
Some quote, unquote “jazz musicians” have mentioned that Rudy Wiedoft inspired them, not what he was playing so much as just what could be done on the instrument. Do you remember him?

Oh, definitely. He let you know what could be done on the instrument, and he let you know that he could do it, you know. It was purely technique, which was a dazzling technique for the time. Gee, I mean, there was also a player around at that time that I think came from Lexington, Kentucky, another one that nobody around today would probably remember or would have heard of, and his name was Leonard Fields, and he was a fantastic player.
